title: Sign-stealing espionage ring exposed

realPrecedents.summary: Michigan staffer Connor Stalions ran an in-person scouting scheme to steal opponents' signals. Commissioner Tony Petitti suspended Jim Harbaugh for the last three regular-season games (2023-11-10) under the Big Ten Sportsmanship Policy, before the NCAA finished its case. Michigan dropped its lawsuit when Harbaugh accepted.
NCAA penalties against Michigan (August 2025): fines estimated at $20M+ tied to postseason revenue, long show-causes for Stalions and Harbaugh, and a suspension for Sherrone Moore. No postseason ban.

description: Reports reveal a member's staffer bought tickets to rivals' games to film signals. Rivals demand immediate league action before the NCAA finishes, and the accused school threatens to sue if you act early.
typicalChoices: Suspend the head coach now under the sportsmanship policy (Petitti model)
Fine the school and wait for the NCAA
Negotiate a self-imposed penalty with the school's president
note: The 2025 NCAA penalty dollar figures are estimates from coverage and not re-verified.

title: Institutional abuse or sexual-assault cover-up at a member

realPrecedents.summary: Penn State: Jerry Sandusky charged. Joe Paterno fired. The 2012 Freeh Report led to an NCAA consent decree ($60M fine, 4-year bowl ban, vacated wins, later restored in 2015). The Big Ten redirected Penn State's bowl revenue share (about $13M over 4 years) to charities.

Baylor: the Pepper Hamilton review found football players' sexual assaults were mishandled. Art Briles fired, Ken Starr removed. The Big 12 board voted (2017) to withhold 25% of Baylor's future distributions until reforms were verified.
Michigan State: Larry Nassar abuse. President Lou Anna Simon resigned. $500M settlement.

description: An investigation shows a member's athletic department ignored or covered up abuse. Media and lawmakers ask what the conference will do. Members fear contagion, and the member's board resists outside oversight.
typicalChoices: Withhold part of the member's distributions until reforms are verified (Big 12/Baylor model)
Redirect postseason revenue to victims' charities (Big Ten/Penn State model)
Defer to the NCAA and courts

title: Academic fraud scandal (fake classes, ghostwritten work)

realPrecedents.summary: UNC: the Wainstein report found 18 years of 'paper classes' in African and Afro-American Studies used to keep athletes eligible. The NCAA (2017) ruled it couldn't find academic violations. The accreditor put UNC on probation (2015).
Florida State: an academic cheating case led the NCAA to vacate 12 of Bobby Bowden's wins.

description: A whistleblower shows athletes were steered into no-show classes. Academic peers in the conference (AAU members) are embarrassed. Penalties could hit a flagship brand.
typicalChoices: Push for vacated wins and fines
Stay quiet and let the accreditor handle it
Create a conference-wide academic integrity standard

title: Booster cash and recruiting violations case

realPrecedents.summary: SMU 'death penalty': the football program was shut down after continued booster payments. The Southwest Conference's credibility collapsed.
Miami: booster Nevin Shapiro's claims of benefits to dozens of athletes. The NCAA's own investigative misconduct undercut the case.
Ole Miss: NCAA notice of allegations. Hugh Freeze resigned (July 2017). 2-year bowl ban. Bitter fallout with Mississippi State over recruit testimony.

description: An NCAA notice of allegations names boosters at a member. The in-state rival is implicated as a witness, and the rivalry turns into a legal and political fight.
typicalChoices: Support the member through the NCAA process
Impose conference penalties (bowl revenue, TV appearances)
Mediate between the feuding in-state members

title: FBI bribery probe of basketball recruiting

realPrecedents.summary: FBI arrests (2017-09-26) of assistant coaches (Auburn's Chuck Person, Arizona's Book Richardson, Oklahoma State's Lamont Evans, USC's Tony Bland) and Adidas executives. Louisville fired Rick Pitino. Later fallout: LSU's Will Wade, Kansas, NC State, Arizona's Sean Miller. Most cases ended in the 2023 independent process (IARP) with probation, not bans.
Louisville's escort scandal (Katina Powell) led to the 2013 national title being vacated in 2018.

description: Federal agents arrest assistant coaches at two members over shoe-company payments to recruits. Wiretaps may name more schools. Your basketball tournament and TV partners are nervous.
typicalChoices: Hire outside counsel to audit every member's basketball program
Suspend implicated coaches from conference events

title: Point-shaving or game-fixing indictment

realPrecedents.summary: Boston College basketball point-shaving scheme with Lucchese crime family associates (Henry Hill).
Arizona State's Stevin 'Hedake' Smith shaved points in Pac-10 games for bookmakers.

After 2025 NCAA findings at Fresno State, San Jose State and New Orleans, a January 2026 federal indictment charged fixers and about two dozen former college players across many D-I programs. Details not re-verified.

description: Integrity monitors flag unusual betting on a member's games, and federal prosecutors unseal charges naming current or former players. Sportsbooks pull your conference's games off the board.
typicalChoices: Lobby footprint states to ban college player props
Suspend implicated players and coaches pending investigation
Hold a press conference showing you are cooperating
note: Use a G6 or mid-major multiplier of about 3x. The 2026 indictment details are not verified.

title: Athletes or staff caught betting (no fixing)

realPrecedents.summary: Iowa and Iowa State: a state investigation charged about two dozen athletes with underage or college-sports betting (QB Hunter Dekkers). Charges were later largely dropped because the geofencing search was questionable.
Alabama baseball coach Brad Bohannon was fired after suspicious bets on an Alabama game at a Cincinnati sportsbook.

description: State regulators find dozens of a member's athletes placed bets, some on their own school's other teams. Rosters are hit mid-season.
typicalChoices: Seek NCAA reinstatement leniency for minor bettors
Require gambling education across the league

title: Hazing and abuse inside a football program

realPrecedents.summary: Northwestern: a hazing investigation led to Pat Fitzgerald's firing (July 2023) after a reversed 2-game suspension. Lawsuits followed, and Fitzgerald's wrongful-termination suit was later settled.

description: A student newspaper reports widespread hazing. The president first gives the coach a light suspension, then reverses under backlash. Lawsuits name the conference as a defendant over its oversight.
typicalChoices: Issue a league-wide hazing policy and audit
Publicly urge the member to act

title: Head coach fired for personal misconduct

realPrecedents.summary: Alabama fired Mike Price before he coached a game, after a strip-club incident.
Arkansas fired Bobby Petrino after a motorcycle crash exposed an affair with an employee he had hired.
Michigan fired Sherrone Moore for cause in December 2025 over an inappropriate relationship with a staff member. Criminal charges followed.

description: A star coach at a flagship member is fired for cause days before a big game or the postseason. The story overshadows your championship week.
typicalChoices: Make a statement on conduct standards
Offer the member's interim coach league support

title: College Sports Commission cap-circumvention investigation

realPrecedents.summary: In October 2026 the CSC was questioning 5-10 P4 programs, including playoff contenders, over third-party payments that may get around the $21.5M revenue-share cap. By November 11 it had more than a dozen active cases and no penalties.
The SEC proposed its own tiered fines ('luxury tax') on roster spending above about $50.5M, and the Big Ten set a combined limit of about $49M.

description: CSC investigators visit a member that is a playoff contender. Rivals leak that its collective is paying 'marketing' deals far above market value. A penalty could cost your league a CFP bid.
typicalChoices: Advocate for the member in arbitration
Impose a conference fine first to pre-empt harsher CSC penalties

title: Collective defaults on an NIL promise, and the recruit sues

realPrecedents.summary: QB Jaden Rashada sued Florida coach Billy Napier and boosters after a reported $13.85M NIL package collapsed in 2023.

description: A top recruit sues a member's coach and collective for fraud over unpaid NIL guarantees. Discovery could expose the league's whole NIL ecosystem.
typicalChoices: Push the member to settle quietly
Use it to promote standardized league contracts

title: League executive overrides replay officials

realPrecedents.summary: In Washington State vs. USC, Pac-12 general counsel Woodie Dixon reportedly influenced a targeting review from the replay booth. Leaked internal reports led to an independent review and damaged Larry Scott's tenure.

description: Leaked internal reports show a conference executive, not the officials, decided a key replay review. The losing school's coach goes public.
typicalChoices: Order an independent review and publish it

title: Blown call decides a marquee game

realPrecedents.summary: Colorado beat Missouri on a 'fifth down' that officials miscounted. Colorado went on to share the national title.
Oregon beat Oklahoma after a botched onside-kick ruling and a replay error. The Pac-10 suspended the crew, and OU president David Boren asked that the game be removed from the record books.

description: A clear officiating and replay error decides a game with playoff stakes. The losing school's president demands the result be voided and the crew fired.
typicalChoices: Suspend the crew and apologize publicly
Privately compensate the wronged school (e.g., bowl priority)

title: Brawl, flag-planting or field storming

realPrecedents.summary: Michigan State players assaulted Michigan players in the Michigan Stadium tunnel. Criminal charges and suspensions followed.
A flag-planting brawl and pepper spray after Michigan's upset at Ohio State. The Big Ten fined both schools $100,000.
Vanderbilt fans tore down the goalposts after beating No. 1 Alabama and dumped them in the Cumberland River. Fined under the SEC's escalating field-storming policy.

description: A rivalry game ends in a melee or a dangerous field storm. Video goes viral. Rival fan bases demand suspensions.
typicalChoices: Suspend players for the next game, possibly a title game

title: Your undefeated champion is left out of the playoff

realPrecedents.summary: TCU and Baylor (co-champions under the Big 12's 'One True Champion' slogan) were left out of the first 4-team CFP. The Big 12 brought back its championship game in 2017.
13-0 ACC champion Florida State was left out of the CFP (QB injury cited). Florida politicians were furious, and it fed FSU's lawsuit against the ACC.

description: The selection committee leaves your champion out, or seeds it badly. The member's president blames your schedule and the league's weak brand, and talks about leaving.
typicalChoices: Lobby the CFP Management Committee for format changes
Add or restructure the championship game or schedule
Offer the member extra revenue to calm it

title: Members' secret talks with a rival league leak

realPrecedents.summary: The Houston Chronicle (Brent Zwerneman, 2021-07-21) revealed Texas and Oklahoma's secret talks with the SEC. Big 12 commissioner Bob Bowlsby accused ESPN of tortious interference. The SEC invited both on 2021-07-30.

description: A beat writer reports two of your flagship members have been negotiating with a rival league for months. You learn about it from Twitter.
typicalChoices: Go public and accuse the rival league or TV partner
Start your own expansion talks immediately
Ask the state legislatures to step in

title: President's insulting remarks leak

realPrecedents.summary: A recording of Ohio State president Gordon Gee's December 2012 remarks mocking Notre Dame, the SEC and Louisville was obtained by the AP. He retired soon after.

description: A recording surfaces of a member president mocking another member, a rival league, or you. Relationships across the board sour.
typicalChoices: Use it as leverage in a pending vote

title: Media contract or internal memo leaks

realPrecedents.summary: Terms of the Pac-12's Apple streaming proposal leaked (revenue tied to subscriptions, not guaranteed). Members left within days.
FSU's lawsuit made the ACC-ESPN grant-of-rights and contract terms public.
CBS published parts of an internal College Sports Commission memo about long-term cap-evasion investigations.

description: A confidential term sheet or memo turns up in the press. Members feel misled, rival leagues know your numbers, and your negotiating position is gone.
typicalChoices: Get ahead of it with a full briefing to members
Speed up the deal before it falls apart

title: Hurricane shuts down a member's campus for a semester

realPrecedents.summary: After Hurricane Katrina, Tulane closed for the fall. The football team was based at Louisiana Tech and played 'home' games elsewhere. Tulane later cut 8 sports in its renewal plan.

description: A major hurricane makes a member's campus and stadium unusable. Teams need temporary homes, schedules collapse, and the school's finances are shaken.
typicalChoices: Host displaced teams at other members' facilities
Create an emergency relief fund from league revenue
Waive the school's dues or penalties
Seek NCAA waivers on eligibility and minimum sports

title: Storm forces a marquee game to be moved or canceled

realPrecedents.summary: Hurricane Matthew: Florida postponed LSU at Florida. After a public standoff, SEC commissioner Greg Sankey brokered a move to Baton Rouge in November, and Florida gave up a home game.
Hurricane Irma forced rescheduling across Florida, including Miami at Florida State.
Hurricane Helene devastated western North Carolina. App State games were postponed.

description: A storm threatens a key late-season game. Both schools have competing interests (home revenue, playoff tiebreakers), and TV wants a decision now.
typicalChoices: Order the game moved to the other team's stadium
Cancel it and use no-contest tiebreakers
Let the schools work it out
note: For conferences in the Southeast or Gulf. Use about 0.03 for others.

title: Tornado devastates a member's town

realPrecedents.summary: An EF4 tornado hit Tuscaloosa on 2011-04-27, killing dozens, including an Alabama football player.

description: A tornado kills residents and damages campus. The league organizes relief and plans memorials.
typicalChoices: Waive costs for the affected school

title: Pandemic: postpone or play?

realPrecedents.summary: The NCAA canceled the 2020 basketball tournaments (2020-03-12). The Big Ten postponed fall football on 2020-08-11 under new commissioner Kevin Warren, faced parent protests, a players' lawsuit and a call from President Trump, then reversed on 2020-09-16. The Pac-12 also reversed. The SEC, ACC and Big 12 played.

description: A public-health emergency forces a decision on the season. Medical advisers split, presidents split, rival leagues decide differently, and every option risks backlash.
typicalChoices: Wait and see what rival leagues do

title: Campus violence kills athletes

realPrecedents.summary: Three Virginia football players were killed in a campus shooting (2022-11-13). The season finale against Virginia Tech was canceled.
A Michigan State campus shooting (2023-02-13) led to postponed games and league-wide tributes.

description: A tragedy hits a member campus. Games must be canceled or postponed and tributes organized, and the affected school's standings and bowl status need handling.
typicalChoices: Cancel the game and adjust tiebreakers
League-wide tributes and moments of silence

title: Coast-to-coast travel burden revolt

realPrecedents.summary: Stanford, Cal and SMU joined the ACC (Cal and Stanford about 2,500+ miles from most members). Olympic-sport travel costs and missed class time drew athlete and faculty complaints.
The Big Ten's West Coast schools (USC, UCLA, Oregon, Washington) faced multiple cross-country trips and non-revenue sport scheduling problems.

description: Athletes, coaches and faculty senates at your far-flung members complain about travel. Women's and Olympic teams are on planes every week, and a viral athlete video makes it national news.
typicalChoices: Create regional pods for Olympic sports
Fund charter flights from league revenue
Cut conference games in non-revenue sports
note: Only when member geography is spread across more than 2 time zones.

title: Hawaii travel subsidy dispute

realPrecedents.summary: Hawaii joined the MWC for football (and the Big West for other sports). Travel-subsidy arrangements in which opponents get compensation for trips to Honolulu became a recurring cost-sharing issue.

description: Members complain about subsidizing trips to a remote member, and the remote member threatens to leave without them.
typicalChoices: Raise the subsidy from league revenue
Make the remote member pay more
Schedule fewer trips to the remote member

title: Team plane or bus crash

realPrecedents.summary: Southern Airways Flight 932 crashed, killing 75, including most of the Marshall football team.
An Oklahoma State men's basketball team plane crash killed 10.

description: A catastrophic travel accident. Extremely rare but defining. The league's response shapes its identity for decades.

title: Member sues the conference

realPrecedents.summary: Maryland left for the Big Ten. The ACC sued to collect its $52.3M exit fee and they settled in 2014 for $31.4M.
Washington State and Oregon State sued the Pac-12 for board control after 10 members left, and won (Whitman County, WA).
FSU (December 2023) and Clemson (March 2024) sued the ACC over the grant of rights and exit fees. Settled March 2025 with lower exit fees and brand-based revenue distribution.

description: A member's trustees vote to sue the conference in their home county court to escape the grant of rights or to seize governance control. Your lawyers rush to file first in a friendlier venue.
typicalChoices: File a pre-emptive suit in the league's home state
Offer a revenue-model concession to settle
Rally the other members to sanction the plaintiff
Let it play out in court

title: Member uses state courts to roster ineligible players

realPrecedents.summary: LSU, under coach Lane Kiffin, used Louisiana court rulings to try to roster former NFL-contract players (Dae'Quan Wright, Zxavian Harris) and then basketball's RJ Luis Jr. The SEC sued LSU in federal court (2026-09-03) and scheduled a 2026-12-03 vote on terminating LSU's membership (needs 2/3 of the other 15). Louisiana AG Liz Murrill represents LSU.

description: A flagship member gets a home-state injunction barring the conference from punishing it for playing athletes your rules say are ineligible. Rivals call it cheating and demand action.
typicalChoices: Sue the member in federal court
Change the rule so the defiance doesn't matter
note: Probability goes up when the member is in a state with a shield law or high statePoliticalPressure.

title: Member's finances implode

realPrecedents.summary: Arizona found a cash-reserve shortfall of over $200M under President Robert Robbins, partly from athletics loans. Arizona moved to the Big 12 that summer. Robbins later stepped down.

description: A member's president admits a huge budget hole. The athletic department owes the university tens of millions. The school may not be able to pay revenue share or stay competitive, and the state board takes control.
typicalChoices: Help broker a state or private-capital bailout

title: Board overrules its president, or a president bypasses the board

realPrecedents.summary: After Jordan McNair's heatstroke death, Maryland's regents kept coach DJ Durkin. President Wallace Loh fired him the next day anyway, and the regents' chair resigned.
UCLA Chancellor Gene Block negotiated the Big Ten move without telling the UC Regents. The Regents and Gov. Newsom objected and imposed conditions.
Michigan's regents publicly opposed the Big Ten's $2.4B private-capital deal and accused Commissioner Petitti of coercion, effectively vetoing it.

description: A member president promised you a vote, but the trustees or regents publicly reverse it, or a president commits the school without board approval. A deal you need unanimity for is in jeopardy.
typicalChoices: Rework the deal to win the holdout

title: Boosters force a $50M coaching buyout

realPrecedents.summary: An early-season firing spree: Penn State fired James Franklin (buyout about $49M), LSU fired Brian Kelly (about $54M), and Florida fired Billy Napier, while member schools were also paying revenue share.

description: A member fires its coach mid-season under donor pressure and owes a huge buyout. It then asks the league for a distribution advance and argues against tougher spending limits.
typicalChoices: Propose league-wide buyout caps or mid-season firing rules
note: Buyout figures are approximate reported values.

title: Surprise defection of your marquee members

realPrecedents.summary: USC and UCLA announced their move to the Big Ten (2022-06-30), blindsiding Pac-12 commissioner George Kliavkoff, who had just turned down a merger with the Big 12.

description: With no warning, your two biggest-market members announce they're leaving for a rival league in two years. Media partners call your negotiation team. The remaining members start making calls of their own.
typicalChoices: Rush to sign a media extension
Raid a G6 or mid-level league for replacements
Lock remaining members into a grant of rights immediately

title: Rival commissioner raids your league

realPrecedents.summary: The ACC took Miami, Virginia Tech and later Boston College from the Big East. The Big East schools sued.
The Big Ten took Maryland (from the ACC) and Rutgers (from the Big East) for TV markets.
Brett Yormark's Big 12 signed Colorado (2023-07-27), then Arizona, ASU and Utah (2023-08-04) as the Pac-12's media talks failed.

description: A rival commissioner publicly says he's 'open for business' and invites three of your members on a deadline. Your members want a counteroffer within days.
typicalChoices: Offer an unequal revenue split to keep stars
note: If the PCSA is enacted, multiply by about 0.25 for P4-to-P4 moves (20/22 cap plus 3-year independence).

title: Poaching-penalty legal war

realPrecedents.summary: The Pac-12 recruited five MWC schools despite a 'poaching penalty' in their 2024 scheduling agreement. Lawsuits and countersuits over penalties and exit fees followed.

description: You poached schools from a league that has an anti-poaching clause with you. It sues for millions, and the departing schools' exit fees are disputed too.
typicalChoices: Fight the suit as an unlawful restraint
Cover the new members' exit fees

title: The two biggest leagues form a governing duopoly

realPrecedents.summary: The 'Alliance' (Big Ten, ACC, Pac-12) formed after Texas and OU defected, but collapsed within a year.
The SEC and Big Ten created a joint advisory group (February 2024). The 2024 CFP agreement gave them control over format decisions from 2026 and the largest revenue shares.

description: The two richest leagues announce a joint group to set playoff format and policy and invite you to 'consult'. Your presidents ask whether you're still at the table.
typicalChoices: Ally with the other leagues left out
Ask to join the group on their terms
Lobby Congress or the White House

title: Rival league takes a private-capital infusion

realPrecedents.summary: The Big Ten negotiated a $2.4B investment from UC Investments for 10% of 'Big Ten Enterprises'. It was paused in November 2025 after Michigan and USC objected and Congress pushed back.

description: A rival league reportedly closes a multibillion-dollar private-equity deal, giving each member an up-front check. Your members ask why you don't have one.
typicalChoices: Warn members about loss of control and tax risk
Wait to see if Congress or the IRS act

title: Member's coach leaves before the playoff

realPrecedents.summary: Lane Kiffin left Ole Miss for LSU (2025-11-30) before Ole Miss's CFP run. Ole Miss promoted Pete Golding. The Senate's 2026 bill reportedly discussed limits on mid-season coaching moves.

description: A rival member hires away your playoff-bound member's coach days before the postseason. The jilted school demands league rules against mid-season poaching.
typicalChoices: Propose an intra-league mid-season no-poach rule
Penalize the poaching member's media exposure

title: Merger proposal from a weakened league

realPrecedents.summary: After USC and UCLA left, the Big 12 and Pac-12 explored mergers, and Kliavkoff declined. A year later the Pac-12 collapsed.
The Pac-12's remaining two members and the MWC discussed a merger and scheduling, then chose a Pac-12 rebuild through MWC defections instead.

description: A struggling league's commissioner proposes a merger or a 'reverse merger' takeover of your charter. Your weaker members like the stability, and your stronger members fear dilution.
typicalChoices: Accept on your terms (absorb selected schools)
Use it as leverage with TV partners

title: Partner's extension option or early-renewal window

realPrecedents.summary: Yormark's Big 12 signed an early extension with ESPN and FOX through 2030-31 (about $2.28B), getting ahead of the Pac-12 and leaving it with a shrunken market.
ESPN exercised its option to extend the ACC deal through 2036, keeping the grant of rights in place during the FSU and Clemson settlement.

description: Your partner's option or exclusive window is approaching. Renewing early gives certainty at a lower price. Going to market gives a possibly higher price, at the risk of being left without a partner.
typicalChoices: Bring in a streamer as a second partner

title: Incumbent network lowballs you

realPrecedents.summary: ESPN's reported offer to the post-USC/UCLA Pac-12 came in far below expectations (about $30M per school was reported). Kliavkoff's slow talks and final Apple streaming offer triggered the league's collapse.

description: Your incumbent partner's renewal offer is well below what members were told to expect. Rival commissioners are already calling your members.

title: Streaming-first or owned-network gamble

realPrecedents.summary: The Pac-12 Networks launched fully league-owned under Larry Scott. They never reached DirecTV carriage, and per-school payouts fell behind the Big Ten and SEC networks.
The Pac-12's Apple proposal tied revenue to subscriptions. Members rejected the uncertainty and left.

description: A tech company or your own network offers big upside but no guaranteed money and little linear exposure. Members are split between growth and certainty.
typicalChoices: Take the streamer's deal with a guaranteed floor
Hybrid: linear partner plus a streaming package

title: Carriage blackout during the season

realPrecedents.summary: The Disney-Charter dispute blacked out ESPN networks for millions of Spectrum customers during the first weeks of the season.
The YouTube TV-Disney carriage dispute blacked out ESPN and ABC during the college football season.

description: A distributor drops your partner's channels in the middle of the season. Rivalry games are unavailable in member states, and fans and governors complain to you.
typicalChoices: Push your partner to stream the games free
note: The 2025 YouTube TV-Disney blackout timing is from memory.

title: Celebrity coach drives a ratings boom

realPrecedents.summary: Deion Sanders's Colorado started 3-0 with record audiences (the late-night Colorado-Colorado State game drew about 9M on ESPN), then finished 4-8, still a top TV draw. It helped push Colorado back to the Big 12.

description: A celebrity coach makes a mid-level member must-see TV. Partners want more prime-time windows for them, and other members resent the favoritism.
typicalChoices: Use the buzz in media negotiations
Build a league-wide content strategy around it

title: Perennial loser becomes a title contender

realPrecedents.summary: Indiana under Curt Cignetti went from historic doormat to a CFP team in 2024 and national champion in 2025-26 (beating Miami for the title), with Heisman winner Fernando Mendoza.

description: A low-brand member suddenly becomes a national power. Its president gains standing, the TV pecking order shifts, and blue-blood members feel threatened.
note: Indiana beating Miami for the 2025-26 title and Mendoza winning the Heisman are from training data (through mid-2026). The title-game matchup is confirmed by a CBS headline, but the score was not re-verified.

title: Women's basketball superstar boom

realPrecedents.summary: Caitlin Clark's Iowa: the 2024 women's final (South Carolina-Iowa) drew about 18.9M viewers, more than the men's final. That set off a re-evaluation of WBB media rights.

description: A member's women's basketball star breaks viewership records. Partners want to buy WBB rights separately, and Title IX advocates demand more investment.
typicalChoices: Unbundle WBB rights for a separate sale
Move the WBB tournament to a bigger venue or market

title: Ratings slump: bad TV windows and weak distribution

realPrecedents.summary: 'Pac-12 After Dark': late kickoffs on the West Coast and limited distribution of the Pac-12 Networks hurt national exposure and recruiting perception.

description: Your games are stuck in late or obscure windows. National audiences and partners' valuations fall, and members blame the media strategy.
typicalChoices: Move kickoffs earlier despite heat or attendance problems
Sign a secondary partner for reach

title: Mid-major Cinderella run in March

realPrecedents.summary: 16-seed UMBC beat 1-seed Virginia, the first 16-over-1 upset.
15-seed Saint Peter's (MAAC) reached the Elite Eight.
9-seed FAU reached the Final Four, and the American soon invited the school.

description: A low-seeded member (or a non-member in your footprint) makes a deep tournament run, bringing NCAA units, national buzz, and a coach every power program wants to hire.
typicalChoices: Invite the school to your league (if a non-member)
Help the member keep its coach
Use the run in media pitches
note: Positive event. For non-P4 conferences use about 0.25.

title: G6 football crasher

realPrecedents.summary: Boise State beat Oklahoma in the Fiesta Bowl with trick plays (January 2007). The same year, FCS Appalachian State beat No. 5 Michigan.
Cincinnati became the first G6 team in the 4-team CFP, then got a Big 12 invitation.
Boise State (Ashton Jeanty) earned a top-4 seed and a bye in the first 12-team CFP. It joined the Pac-12 in 2026.

description: A G6 program goes undefeated or wins a New Year's Six game. Power leagues start courting it, and its current league's stability is at risk.
typicalChoices: Schedule it as a non-conference partner

title: Member cuts Olympic sports (and faces a Title IX fight)

realPrecedents.summary: During COVID, Stanford announced cuts to 11 varsity sports and reversed in 2021 after lawsuits and alumni pressure. Minnesota, Iowa, East Carolina, William & Mary and Dartmouth also cut sports. Iowa had to reinstate women's swimming after a Title IX suit.
Revenue sharing under the House settlement (up to $20.5M) put pressure on non-revenue budgets across D-I.

description: A member says it will drop several Olympic sports to fund revenue sharing. That leaves your league below the sport-sponsorship minimum for its automatic bid, and Title IX lawyers circle.
typicalChoices: Subsidize the sport from league revenue
Change sponsorship minimums or add affiliate members
Lobby for federal Olympic-sport protections (PCSA bans cuts)

title: Member drops out of Division I

realPrecedents.summary: Centenary College of Louisiana moved from D-I to D-III to cut costs.
Saint Francis University (PA) announced a move from D-I (NEC) to D-III, citing the economics after the House settlement.

description: A small member says D-I is no longer affordable. You lose a member, an automatic-bid count, and scheduling slots.
typicalChoices: Offer financial relief to keep them
note: Mostly for non-P4 conferences. For low-major conferences use about 0.08. The year of the Saint Francis (PA) move to D-III is from memory and not re-verified.

title: Athlete wins an eligibility injunction mid-season

realPrecedents.summary: Diego Pavia (Vanderbilt) won a preliminary injunction (2024-12-18) on counting JUCO seasons. The NCAA issued a blanket waiver.
Charles Bediako (former G League) sought to return to Alabama. Ohio's Borovicanin case and Gov. DeWine's order gave class-of-2022 athletes a fifth year, and the NCAA sued DeWine.

description: A state judge orders a member to play an athlete your rules call ineligible. Rival members ask whether results will be vacated if the ruling is later reversed (the NCAA's restitution rule).
typicalChoices: Follow the order and protect the results
Warn that results may be vacated

title: Departing members negotiate their exit fee

realPrecedents.summary: The ACC and Maryland settled the $52.3M exit-fee fight for $31.4M.
Texas and OU paid the Big 12 a combined $100M to leave in 2024 instead of 2025 (February 2023 settlement).

description: Departing members offer a lump sum to leave early. Holding out maximizes money. Settling early gives certainty and lets you start rebuilding.
typicalChoices: Hold for the full fee and litigate
Trade the fee for scheduling or media concessions

title: Title IX suit over revenue-share allocation

realPrecedents.summary: Title IX objectors appealed the House settlement, arguing the back-pay split (mostly football and men's basketball) and the revenue-share allocations discriminate. Education Department guidance flipped twice (January to February 2025).
Critics argue the Senate-passed PCSA still lets schools concentrate pay on football despite its Title IX savings clause.

description: Women's team athletes at a member sue, saying the school's 80/10/5/5 revenue split violates Title IX. The suit names the conference's revenue-share policy.
typicalChoices: Adopt a league-wide minimum share for women's sports

title: New antitrust class action targets conference rules

realPrecedents.summary: NCAA v. Alston: the Supreme Court ruled 9-0 against limits on education-related benefits.
House v. NCAA settlement: about $2.8B in damages plus revenue sharing.

description: Plaintiffs' firms sue the NCAA and your conference over a rule (roster limits, transfer limits, the cap itself). Discovery is costly, and the antitrust cover depends on whether Congress acts.
typicalChoices: Lobby for the PCSA safe harbor
Coordinate defense with the other P4

title: Legislature demands a package deal

realPrecedents.summary: Texas politicians (Gov. Ann Richards, Lt. Gov. Bob Bullock) made sure Baylor and Texas Tech joined Texas and Texas A&M in the new Big 12.
Gov. Mark Warner pressured UVA to back Virginia Tech's admission to the ACC.

description: You're about to admit a flagship. Its state legislature threatens budget retaliation unless you also admit an in-state rival you don't want.
typicalChoices: Offer the rival a scheduling deal or affiliate status

title: Governor issues an order overriding NCAA or league rules

realPrecedents.summary: Ohio Gov. Mike DeWine's EO 2026-04D (2026-10-13) let Ohio schools give class-of-2022 athletes a fifth year. The NCAA sued him in federal court.

description: A governor in your footprint signs an order giving that state's members an eligibility or NIL advantage. Other members demand the league neutralize it.
typicalChoices: Adopt a matching league rule for all members
Ban the advantage under league bylaws (lawsuit risk)

title: Federal college-sports bill reaches a vote

realPrecedents.summary: House leaders pulled the SCORE Act from the floor hours before a December 2025 vote, and again in May 2026.

The Senate passed the Protect College Sports Act 77-22 (2026-09-28), with a 20-school P4 cap and a 3-year independence rule for P4 switchers. A House lame-duck vote is set for the week of 2026-12-08 after Democrats swept the midterms.

description: Congress is days from voting on a bill that would freeze conference sizes, give antitrust protection and preempt state laws. Your members split by their realignment ambitions, and lawmakers want your public endorsement.
typicalChoices: Lobby to change the realignment terms

title: The White House gets involved

realPrecedents.summary: President Trump called Big Ten commissioner Kevin Warren (2020-09-01) to push for a fall season. The Big Ten reversed two weeks later.
A presidential commission with Nick Saban and Cody Campbell was floated in May 2025, then replaced by EO 14322 (2025-07-24).
EO 14400 (2026-04-03) tied federal grant responsibility to NCAA-rule compliance and pushed 5-year eligibility.

description: The president publicly pressures your league on a decision (playing during a crisis, eligibility, NIL) or invites you to the White House. Members' home-state politics split along party lines.
typicalChoices: Comply and accept the photo op
Use the moment to push your agenda

title: Athlete boycott or protest

realPrecedents.summary: Missouri football players threatened to boycott a game over campus racial climate. System president Tim Wolfe resigned within days.
Minnesota players boycotted bowl preparations over teammates' suspensions in a sexual-assault case.
Pac-12 players' '#WeAreUnited' demands over COVID safety and revenue sharing.

description: Athletes at one or more members threaten to sit out a televised game unless demands are met (safety, pay, social issues). TV partners and presidents call you.

title: Athlete dies in training or competition

realPrecedents.summary: Loyola Marymount star Hank Gathers collapsed and died during the WCC tournament. The tournament was suspended.
Maryland's Jordan McNair died of heatstroke after a supervised workout. External reviews followed and coach DJ Durkin was fired.
13 Iowa football players were hospitalized with rhabdomyolysis after a workout.

description: An athlete dies or several are hospitalized after a workout. Families, media and lawmakers demand league-wide health standards and independent medical authority.
